sections.title: The same split you already know
sections.content: egyet behaves just like the igekötők (bemegy, felkel, elkezd) you already met — glued to the front in a plain statement, but sent behind the verb under negation, because nem needs the spot right in front of the verb. So egyetértek becomes nem értek egyet, not "nem egyetértek", exactly the same swap as bemegyek becoming nem megyek be.

items.spanish: Nem értek egyet veled, szerintem a másik terv jobb.
items.english: I don't agree with you, in my opinion the other plan is better.

items.spanish: Szerintem finom volt a vacsora. Szerintem is!
items.english: In my opinion dinner was tasty. I think so too!

sections.content: Szerintem is ("I think so too") and Szerintem nem ("I don't think so") are the shortest way to echo someone without repeating their whole sentence — is ("also, too") reuses the same little word you already know from én is.
